title: How to restrict a field that allowed multiple users to accept only one owner?
summary: See how to restrict a field that allowed multiple users to accept only one owner in Jestor.
body_text: In Jestor 's multiple-users field, you can enable an option that forces the selection of just one owner per record — useful when a process, like a sales opportunity, needs a single clear owner instead of several people responsible at once. Why does restricting to a single owner prevent confusion in some processes? Certain processes, like a sales opportunity, work better with a single, clearly defined owner — otherwise it becomes ambiguous who's actually responsible for moving that record forward. Allowing multiple users in those cases can create the sense that "everyone's responsible, so no one is." How to restrict the field to a single user in Jestor? Access the settings for the multiple-users field you want to restrict. Enable the option that forces the selection of just one owner. Save the change — from then on, selecting a new user replaces the previous one, instead of allowing both at once. Before that restriction, it's also possible to manually choose which users show up in the selection list, instead of listing everyone registered on the account. Setting Behavior Multiple users (default) Allows selecting more than one owner Restricted to one user Selecting a new user replaces the previous one Why choose Jestor? Beyond this restriction, the multiple-users field also gained a searchable selector, making it easier to find the right person even on accounts with hundreds of registered users in Jestor . Frequently Asked Questions Can this restriction be undone later? Yes, the field's setting can be reverted to allow multiple users again if needed. Does this affect records already created before the change? The setting applies to the next selections made in that field. Can I limit which users show up in the list, beyond restricting the count? Yes, you can manually choose which users are available for selection in that specific field. Get to know Jestor at jestor.com and discover how to take your company's management to a new level of efficiency and integration.

title: Pathward Recognized Among TIME America’s Best Companies 2026
summary: Pathward has been named to TIME’s inaugural list of America’s Best Companies 2026.
body_text: SIOUX FALLS, S.D. – July 9, 2026 – Pathward Financial , Inc. (Nasdaq: CASH) through its subsidiary, Pathward ®, N.A., (“Bank” or “Pathward”), announced the Bank has been named to TIME’s inaugural list of America’s Best Companies 2026 . TIME published the list in collaboration with Statista, a statistics portal and industry ranking provider. TIME and Statista identified America’s Best Companies 2026 based on three primary dimensions: Employee satisfaction – Based on survey data from about 217,000 verified employees at U.S. companies over the past three years, covering company recommendations and employer ratings across image, atmosphere, working conditions, salary, workplace, and equality. Financial performance – Drawn from Statista's revenue database over the past five years. Companies needed at least $100 million in revenue in 2025. Performance was assessed on multiple metrics: short-term (2023–2025) and long-term (2021–2025) revenue growth (relative and absolute), changes in net income, asset growth, and the evolution of return on assets, all for 2023–2025. Sustainability transparency – Based on an Environmental Social Governance (ESG) index from Statista's ESG database and additional research, covering: Environmental: 2024 carbon emissions intensity and reduction rate versus 2022 Social: share of women on the Board of Directors and disclosure of a human rights policy Governance: presence of a Global Reporting Initiative, aligned Corporate Social Responsibility report, and a compliance/anti-corruption policy The 1,000 highest-scoring companies, which included Pathward, earned recognition as America’s Best Companies 2026 by TIME and Statista. “I am proud of Pathward’s commitment to our purpose, people and sustainable business practices,” said Pathward CEO Brett Pharr. “While many factors contribute to performance, our employees are what sets us apart. This recognition from TIME reflects the dedication of our team and the impact they make every day.” As a bank with scalable infrastructure, deep payments expertise, and a consultative risk and compliance approach, Pathward helps fintechs and other payments innovators launch, grow, and scale responsibly. Pathward’s portfolio of offerings includes card issuing, merchant acquiring and digital payments sponsorship, as well as financial institution solutions, credit solutions and professional tax solutions. The Bank also offers flexible working capital, equipment financing, and structured finance solutions to businesses. Find the complete list of America’s Best Companies 2026 on TIME.com. About Pathward Financial, Inc. Pathward Financial, Inc. (Nasdaq: CASH) is a U.S.-based financial holding company driven by its purpose to power financial inclusion. Through our subsidiary, Pathward ® , N.A., we strive to increase financial availability, choice and opportunity across our Partner Solutions and Commercial Finance business lines. These strategic business lines provide support to individuals and businesses. Learn more at PathwardFinancial.com . title: Bowman Perspectives: What It Takes to Win Federal Grants Across Industries – A Q&A with Bowman’s Grant Writing Team
summary: Bowman has helped local governments secure federal and state grants and low-interest loans ranging from $1 million to $500 million.
body_text: Bowman’s grant writing team is built to work across industries, including local utilities, municipal water & wastewater and transportation . Across those sectors, our team has helped local governments throughout the U.S. secure federal and state grants and low-interest loans ranging from $1 million to $500 million for water, sewer and transportation projects. And because Bowman’s services extend beyond grant support, we stay engaged through design, construction and closeout. We sat down with three of our grant writing subject matter experts—Nick Marcotte, director of water & wastewater , Randy Waltermyer, regional service lead, transportation planning and Todd Chase, director of financial & economic consulting —for a look at how Bowman’s grant writing services set clients up for success across industries and projects. Water & Wastewater: Helping Small Communities Build Big Infrastructure Nick Marcotte, PE | Director of Water & Wastewater Q: For smaller or rural municipalities that feel like they can’t compete with larger applicants, where would you tell them to start? A: There are programs specifically designed for smaller communities, including the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Rural Development and the State Revolving Fund (SRF). USDA funding is only available to municipalities below 10,000 people, and SRF provides grants for small and disadvantaged communities based on criteria like median household income. As long as you’re meeting the requirements, the money is largely there, so you ultimately just need to get in line and follow the right procedures. Q: Once a grant is awarded, how does Bowman help navigate cost changes or gaps between the original estimate and what projects actually cost to build? A: We had projects where estimates were developed in early 2020, and by the time we went to bid in 2024 or 2025, construction costs had increased 40 to 50 percent. Both USDA and the SRF have mechanisms to address this; USDA calls it a cost overrun application. Because Bowman handles both the grant side and the engineering, we help clients navigate those moments by pursuing additional funding or finding efficiencies in scope. T ransportation: Funding a More Resilient Transportation Network Randy Waltermyer, AICP | Regional Service Lead, Transportation Planning Q: What types of transportation projects are currently the strongest fit for available federal and state funding programs? A: Projects that aim to address climate change via infrastructure resiliency are very fundable right now. Climate resiliency transcends all transportation modes and sectors, so the intersection and applicability of resiliency grants is quite broad. Q: What’s a transportation project you’re especially proud of helping fund, and what impact has it had? A: Speaking of climate resiliency, in Pittsburgh, PA there’s a depressed section of I-376 that runs along the Monongahela River. Locally, this section of I-376 is known as “the Bathtub” because when the Monongahela spills its banks, it overwhelms this section of the interstate and impacts the 70,000 vehicles that use it daily. Bowman worked with PennDOT and a team of partners to secure $6.7 million in federal funding to raise the floodwall, enhance pumping capacity and incorporate new warning systems to keep this critical artery open and safe. Construction of these improvements is commencing later this year. Local Utilities: Why a Grant Denial Isn’t the End of the Road Todd Chase, LEED | Director of Financial & Economic Consulting Q: What’s the biggest misconception utility clients have about the grant process before they start working with Bowman? A: Most applicants don’t allow enough time to gather the necessary input and letters of support ahead of a due date. It’s good to budget at least four to six weeks for each submission. Beyond timing, clients should also not be discouraged if they don’t get a grant on the first attempt. Most applicants try multiple times before being awarded a major federal grant. Q: If a client has had a grant application denied, what’s your approach to helping them reapply successfully? A: The first step is always a debrief with the grant-issuing agency to understand specifically how to improve in the next round. Next, try to build up the local match and partnerships with other agencies and private entities. Then, make sure the benefit-cost ratio (BCR) is favorable at a 7% discount rate; this may require value engineering to lower costs and fast-tracking construction. Bowman’s grant services team works across sectors and geographies to help clients identify funding opportunities, build competitive applications and deliver funded projects. To learn more about how Bowman can help secure funding for your next project, contact us at grants@bowman.com . title: Weibo Corporation to Report Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results on August 19, 2026
summary: BEIJING, July 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Weibo Corporation (NASDAQ: WB and HKEX: 9898), a leading social media for people to create, share and discover content, will announce its unaudited financial results for the second quarter 2026 before the U.S. market opens on Wednesday, August 19, 2026.
body_text: BEIJING , July 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Weibo Corporation (NASDAQ: WB and HKEX: 9898), a leading social media for people to create, share and discover content, will announce its unaudited financial results for the second quarter 2026 before the U.S. market opens on Wednesday, August 19, 2026. Following the announcement, Weibo's management team will host a conference call from 7 AM – 8 AM Eastern Time on August 19, 2026 (or 7 PM – 8 PM Hong Kong Time on August 19, 2026) to present an overview of the Company's financial performance and business operations. Participants who wish to dial in to the teleconference must register through the below public participant link. Dial in and instruction will be in the confirmation email upon registering. Participants Registration Link: https://register-conf.media-server.com/register/BI4542e6edec00491e9198327b87da5adb Additionally, a live and archived webcast of this conference call will be available at http://ir.weibo.com . About Weibo Weibo is a leading social media for people to create, share and discover content online. Weibo combines the means of public self-expression in real time with a powerful platform for social interaction, content aggregation and content distribution. Any user can create and post a feed and attach multi-media and long-form content. User relationships on Weibo may be asymmetric; any user can follow any other user and add comments to a feed while reposting. This simple, asymmetric and distributed nature of Weibo allows an original feed to become a live viral conversation stream. Weibo enables its advertising and marketing customers to promote their brands, products and services to users. Weibo offers a wide range of advertising and marketing solutions to companies of all sizes. Weibo generates a substantial majority of its revenues from the sale of advertising and marketing services, including the sale of social display advertisement and promoted marketing offerings. Weibo displays content in a simple information feed format and offers native advertisement that conform to the information feed on our platform. We are continuously refining our social interest graph recommendation engine, which enables our customers to perform people marketing and target audiences based on user demographics, social relationships, interests and behaviors, to achieve greater relevance, engagement and marketing effectiveness. title: Hasbro to Produce New Toys Based on Nintendo’s The Legend of Zelda Franchise
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Hasbro, Inc.'s business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: PDF Version PAWTUCKET, R.I.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Jul. 16, 2026-- Hasbro, a leading games, IP and toy company, today announced a new licensing partnership with Nintendo to create products based on the popular Legend of Zelda franchise. This multi-year collaboration is set to begin in 2027, starting with the first reveals of three 6" scale figures at San Diego Comic Con (July 23-26, 2026). “For decades, The Legend of Zelda franchise has captivated fans through its deep lore, unforgettable characters and enduring sense of discovery,” said Billy Lagor, President Toys and Board Games at Hasbro. “By combining Nintendo’s iconic storytelling with Hasbro’s leadership in action and role-play, we’re delivering toys that invite fans to play, explore and forge their own epic adventures.” Ever since its first title, released in the US in 1987, the Legend of Zelda series has mixed exploration and discovery with action and adventure. Link and Zelda’s eternal battle against Ganondorf forms the centerpiece of these epic tales from the world of Hyrule. About Hasbro Hasbro is a leading games, IP and toy company whose mission is to create joy and community through the magic of play. With 165 years of expertise, Hasbro delivers groundbreaking play experiences and reaches more than 1 billion fans annually around the world, through physical and digital games, video games, toys, licensed consumer products, location-based entertainment, film, TV and more. Through its franchise-first approach, Hasbro unlocks value from both new and legacy IP, including Magic: The Gathering, Dungeons & Dragons, Monopoly, Hasbro Games, Nerf, Transformers, Play-Doh and Peppa Pig, as well as premier partner brands. Powered by its portfolio of thousands of iconic marks and a diversified network of partners and subsidiary studios, Hasbro brings fans together wherever they are, from tabletop to screen. For more than a decade, Hasbro has been consistently recognized for its corporate citizenship, including being named one of the 100 Best Corporate Citizens by 3BL Media, a 2026 JUST Capital Industry Leader, a Brand that Matters by Fast Company, and one of the 50 Most Community-Minded Companies in the U.S. by the Civic 50 for fourteen consecutive years. For more information, visit https://corporate.hasbro.com or follow Hasbro on LinkedIn.
